fact: Capital Ethiopia reports the Ministry of Innovation and Technology leading an Interoperable Digital Government Initiative modelled on Brazilian, UK and German government interoperability frameworks, with an Ethiopian eGovernment Interoperability Framework (EeGIF) Governance and Compliance document attached, and assessing existing directives and laws; it gives no adoption date (as_of is the published date).

The Ministry of Innovation and Technology's guidelines-and-standards library lists EA-2019 Ethiopian Government Interoperability Framework with the status Approved; the page gives no approval date (as_of is the published date, 2019).
The Ministry of Innovation and Technology's 2023 e-government assessment, prepared with the Tony Blair Institute, refers to the approved Ethiopian eGovernment Interoperability Framework (EeGIF).
The assessment finds the E-Services Portal offers no data interoperability features, deviating from the approved EeGIF, and a standalone enterprise architecture not aligned with the national one.
